summary.headline: LT Foods Q2 FY27 revenue rose 17% YoY to INR3,253 crore, but EBITDA margin slipped to 11.0% on freight and brand spend.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue grew 17% YoY to INR3,253 crore, with PAT up 10% to INR180 crore. Gross margin fell to 32.5% from 34.2%, driven by a shift to FOB shipment terms with a related party (EBITDA-neutral) and higher shipping costs, which rose about 40 bps of revenue. Advertising rose to 2.5% of revenue from 1.8% in Q1, and EBITDA margin was 11.0%. Management reiterated a 13-13.5% consolidated EBITDA margin target without a timeline, while Middle East was hit by supply and freight disruption.

financial_highlights.change: +13% YoY; vs INR363 crore in Q1 FY27
vs 11.4% in Q2 FY26 and 11.5% in Q1 FY27

segments.name: Basmati and specialty rice (H1 FY27)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR5,764 crore, +27% YoY, on 11% volume growth; 90% of consolidated revenue. Gross margin 33%, EBITDA margin 12%, with mature markets (India, US, RoW) at 15%.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue mix 29%, grew 24% YoY with volume up 10%. Branded portfolio grew about 8% against category growth of about 1.3%; household reach rose to 67.5 lakh from 56.2 lakh.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Revenue mix 50%, grew 21% YoY or 13% normalised after adjusting for Golden Star.

segments.name: Middle East and RoW
segments.commentary: Revenue mix 9%, grew 25% YoY with strong volume growth. Quarter was hit by supply disruption and a sharp freight cost rise; e-commerce grew strongly.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue mix 12%. Secured new private-label business in Germany and Nordics; UK underperformed on lower mainstream and industrial volume and high operating costs.

segments.name: Organic and ingredients (H1 FY27)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR520 crore vs INR583 crore in H1 FY26 (remodelling). Gross margin 34%, EBITDA margin 6%; segment EBITDA INR22 crore in Q2 vs INR10 crore in Q1.

segments.name: Health and convenience (RTH/RTE/RTC, H1 FY27)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR102 crore, +8% from INR95 crore. RTE +17%, RTC +28%, RTH +7% in rupee terms, ahead of the US RTH capacity commissioning.

segments.name: Standalone (H1 FY27)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,417 crore, +14%; EBITDA INR223 crore, +34%, margin 9.2% vs 7.9%; PAT INR134 crore vs INR108 crore. Q2 standalone revenue +17% to INR1,241 crore; Q2 EBITDA margin 8.3%.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated EBITDA margin target of 13%-13.5% (previously 11.5%-12% for FY27 per analyst); no timeline given as a matter of policy.
Advertising spend to average 2.3% of revenue for FY27 vs 2.1% last year.
Management expects H2 to be similar to H1 in momentum; no explicit revenue or PAT growth number given.
Expects price increases to pass through on new crop; says freight impact on consolidated margin is about 0.4%.
UK Basmati business expected to turn profitable as scale builds, targeted for next year.
Organic business targeted at 10%-11% EBITDA margin within two years.
Tariff refund accounting expected to be clear by year end; partial refund received.
capex_capacity: US ready-to-heat (RTH) facility capacity is being built ahead of commissioning; current RTH investment weighed on margins.
New Madhya Pradesh facility for Nature Bio Foods: first phase expected to commence operations in this financial year.
Organic business is consolidating manufacturing and sourcing (Turkey and other regions), with near-term cost.
Paddy inventory 82,000 tons at INR43/kg average; rice inventory 260,000 tons at INR60/kg average (as of 26 Sep 2026).
Inventory days reduced to 159 days from 187 days; trade payable days fell to 26 from 29.
demand_pricing: Crop '26 paddy prices up about 22%-25% on average, varying by variety; management says crop '25 inventory covers the business plan.
Basmati and specialty value grew 26% vs volume 11.5%, implying about 13% per-ton price/realisation gain including forex.
Forex impact on the top line estimated at 4%-5%; policy is 50% hedged, 50% open.
Daawat average realisation about INR80/kg in October, up about 8% vs Q1 FY27.
Management says price increases have not reduced demand; basmati is about 10 million tons of a roughly 500 million ton rice market (about 2%).
Middle East freight rose by $40-50 per unit to above $200; management says no demand impact seen.
Q2 volume growth 11% YoY and 6% QoQ; value growth 21% YoY and 5% QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: What are current basmati inventory levels and average cost, and what is the procurement strategy for higher-priced crops?
qa_highlights.answer: Paddy stock 82,000 tons at INR43/kg and rice stock 260,000 tons at INR60/kg as of 26 Sep 2026. Management said the inventory matches the business plan and crop '25 is sufficiently covered.

qa_highlights.question: Why did RTC/RTH gross and EBITDA margins decline sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to planned promotions and sampling netted in gross profit, which per management was about INR2 crore for H1.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any revision to FY27 EBITDA guidance from 11.5%-12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not revise guidance. It said freight added about 40 bps and brand investment about 20 bps. CFO reiterated 13%-13.5% consolidated margin, with no timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital release in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it is seasonal, as Q2 is a non-peak procurement period. Cash will be used as procurement resumes in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Are tariff refunds being accounted for?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said partial refunds have been received and discussions with customers are ongoing. Clarity is expected by year end.

qa_highlights.question: Do you benefit from the falling rupee, and how much is forex in the top line?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, as an exporter. The forex impact on the top line is estimated at 4%-5%, included in the reported rupee realisation growth.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from shipping costs (about 40 bps of revenue) and the Middle East supply disruption; management expects the price pass-through to show up in later quarters.
Paddy price inflation of 22%-25% for crop '26; pass-through timing and margin impact (management says historically about ±1%).
Europe and UK profitability: UK volumes below plan and high operating costs; UK profitability targeted for next year.
Organic segment revenue fell to INR520 crore in H1 from INR583 crore; margin recovery to 10%-11% is a two-year target.
Working capital reversal expected as procurement resumes; inventory days 159 days vs 187 days year ago.
Rising finance costs from supplier funding arrangements; higher depreciation from new capitalisations.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term margin and growth, but evasive on timelines and on whether FY27 guidance is revised. Management was direct on the quarter's freight and brand-spend drag but gave few numbers on the Middle East, UK and organic segments.
key_quotes: Against category growth of approximately 1.3%, our branded portfolio grew by nearly around nearly 8%, supporting 140 basis point increase in market share on year-to-date basis.
As a policy, we are not giving any timelines.
So, we are confident on the margin target w13% to 13.5% to 14% of the EBITDA margin on consolidated basis.

adds.what: US ready-to-heat (RTH) facility capacity, being built ahead of commissioning (capacity size not stated)
New Madhya Pradesh facility for Nature Bio Foods, first phase (capacity size not stated)

growth.why: Management reiterated a 13%-13.5% consolidated EBITDA margin target (no timeline) and said H2 momentum will be similar to H1, with no explicit revenue growth number; backing is partial, citing crop '26 price increases of about 22%-25%, Q2 volume up 11% YoY, and the Nature Bio Foods MP plant (first phase in FY27) and US RTH capacity, which has no stated size.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management reiterates a 13%-13.5% consolidated EBITDA margin target with no timeline, against 11.0% in Q2 FY27 and 11.2% in H1; freight (about 40 bps) and brand spend (about 20 bps) are drags, and crop '26 price pass-through is expected in later quarters.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Nature Bio Foods' new Madhya Pradesh plant (first phase) is expected to start in FY27 (Q2 FY27 per brief), and US RTH capacity is being built ahead of commissioning, though neither capacity size is stated.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 volume grew 11% YoY and 6% QoQ, basmati volume grew 11% in H1, and India volume rose 10%; management expects H2 momentum similar to H1, with no explicit volume number given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed, so the read is indirect; the company is already building US RTH capacity and the MP plant, and no new capex has been announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management did not revise FY27 guidance (11.5%-12% per analyst) and gave no explicit revenue or PAT growth number; H1 EBITDA margin was 11.2%, below the target range.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin slipped to 11.0% from 11.5% in Q1 on freight and advertising at 2.5% of revenue, Middle East freight rose by $40-50 per unit to above $200, and UK underperformed; management did not revise guidance, so the risk is latent rather than signalled.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: US RTH capacity is being commissioned ahead of launch and RTC grew 28% and RTE 17% in H1, but no specific new product launch was named.

rows.label: Crop '26 price pass-through
rows.why: Crop '26 paddy prices are up about 22%-25%, price increases are expected to pass through on the new crop, and Daawat realisation rose about 8% to about INR80/kg in October vs Q1 FY27.

rows.label: UK Basmati turns profitable
rows.why: Management targets UK Basmati profitability as scale builds, but UK volumes are below plan and operating costs are high, and no numbers were given.

rows.label: Working capital reversal as procurement resumes
rows.why: Inventory days fell to 159 from 187 and payable days to 26 from 29; management says cash will be used as procurement resumes in coming quarters.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 13%-13.5% margin target and on crop '26 price pass-through, but evasive on timing and on whether FY27 guidance changes; analysts pressed on freight, brand spend and the margin slip to 11.0%.
